deep.reconstruction:
This page has no formulae. It is a prose draft of the opening of Riemann's note 'Ein Beitrag zur Elektrodynamik'. He presented it to the Göttingen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften in February 1858, withdrew it, and it was published posthumously in Poggendorff's Annalen in 1867. The draft title, crossed out, reads approximately 'Zur Theorie der elektrodynamischen Fernwirkungen galvanischer Ströme'.

The text says, in sense: studying the electrodynamic actions of galvanic currents led him to a remark linking the theory of electricity and magnetism with that of light and radiant heat. The far-actions of galvanic currents can be explained if the action of one electric mass on the others is not instantaneous. Instead it propagates to them at a constant speed, equal to the speed of light within observational error. Electrodynamic and electromotive actions of 'galvanic oscillations' then propagate by the same laws as light and radiant heat.

Crossed-out and inserted fragments go further. They hint at the hypothesis that light itself is produced by electrical oscillations, with a crossed-out remark about 'electrical molecular oscillations'. Riemann reserves the decision on such hypothetical oscillations, because 'at present I lack the peace and leisure for it'. The page ends with fragments: 'Ich beziehe/begnüge mich ...', a cancelled line beginning 'Es sei in einem Leiter ...', and notes like 'Mechanischer Theil 2 ...' and 'Lehrbuch Ch.', apparently literature references.

In modern terms, the programme (carried out on the following page and in the published note) is as follows. Poisson's equation ΔU = -4πρ for the electrostatic potential is replaced by the inhomogeneous wave equation ∂²U/∂t² = α²(ΔU + 4πρ). Its solution is the retarded potential U(x,t) = ∫ ρ(x', t - |x-x'|/α)/|x-x'| dV'.

Weber's force law is then recovered to the relevant order from the resulting retarded interaction. The quantities on the next page, the time integrals of F(τ - r/a, τ) and the term (r²/a²) d²(1/r)/(dt ds), are the expansion of the retarded potential to second order in r/a. The identification v = 2√2 e'/c, i = 2√2 (e/c) ds/dt corresponds to Weber's constant c with propagation speed α = c/√2.

Nothing is derived on this page itself. It states the physical claim that the derivation serves.
errors: No computations on this page to check. The physical claim rests on the derivation in the published note. Clausius (1868) criticised that derivation: he argued that an interchange of integrations/limits is unjustified and that the resulting retarded scalar-potential theory is inconsistent with energy conservation. A purely scalar retarded potential does not in fact reproduce full Maxwell–Lorentz electrodynamics. The draft's statement that the actions propagate 'by the same laws as light' is therefore an overstatement by modern standards. Lorenz (1867) and the Liénard–Wiechert potentials with a vector potential supply what is missing.

The parenthetical identification of the propagation speed with the speed of light is empirical: Weber–Kohlrausch c/√2 ≈ 310,740 km/s versus Fizeau's measurement. It is correct within the accuracy of the time.

results.what: Hypothesis that electric action propagates at finite constant speed equal to the speed of light, giving a retarded potential and a link between electrodynamics and optics
results.modern_name: Retarded potential / inhomogeneous wave equation for the scalar potential (d'Alembert equation)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1858, publ. 1867); L. Lorenz (1867); Gauss's 1845 letter to Weber anticipated the idea; Maxwell (1865) for the electromagnetic theory of light

results.what: Draft remark (partly cancelled) that light may be produced by electrical oscillations

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's well-known 1858 note 'Ein Beitrag zur Elektrodynamik', whose opening sentences it almost reproduces. The only new elements are draft variants: the explicit, then partly cancelled, suggestion that light is produced by electrical oscillations, and the personal remark about lacking 'Ruhe und Musse'. These are of biographical and philological interest but not mathematically new.

checkable.asserts: The retarded radial potential f(t-r/a)/r satisfies the homogeneous wave equation u_tt = a^2 Δu away from r=0. This is the basis of Riemann's retarded potential.
Weber–Kohlrausch constant c = 439450 km/s divided by sqrt(2) gives about 310740 km/s. This is Riemann's propagation speed α = c/√2, which he identifies with the speed of light.
Consistency of the next page's unit conversion i = 2√2 (e/c) ds/dt: the current in Weber's units scales with the factor 2√2/c (trivial check).

transcription_corrections: 'Theorie des {+der Elektricität und des+} Magnetismus' should read 'Theorie der Elektricität und des Magnetismus'. The insertion replaces 'des'.
Pencil header 'Riemann 19' (archival) and a crossed-out page number '43' at top right; folio number 65 at right margin.
'Ich bezeuge mich ...' is doubtful; more likely 'Ich beziehe mich' or 'Ich begnüge mich', uncertain.
Bottom lines 'Mechanischer Theil 2 ...' and 'Lehrbuch Ch.' are uncertain bibliographic notes. The cancelled line reads approximately 'Es sei in einem Leiter ... elektrische ...'.
The insertion at right reads 'da es mir für jetzt gegenwärtig an Ruhe und Musse dazu fehlt,' — consistent with the given transcription.
